High level: I think we can get this done quickly with a small compromise. My recommended position:
- Subprocessor notice: Agree to 30 days' prior notice, but add explicit carve-out for emergency security/patching where we provide "as soon as reasonably practicable" notice (no longer than 5 business days). Offer monthly consolidated list + a real-time portal for current subprocessors.
- Opt-out for regulated categories: Allow Acme to object to specific subprocessors for narrowly-defined regulated categories (PII tied to regulated financial/health data). For general-purpose infra (CDN, logging, monitoring) we decline opt-out.
- Access/deletion SLA: Counter with 60 days in the contract, but commit operationally to target 45 days and report SLA metrics in Console.
- SOC2: Provide SOC 2 Type II redacted report and offer a short security questionnaire (we already have standard pack).

If you take that back to Sarah, propose the carve-outs in writing and provide the SOC2 + subprocessor portal link. We should avoid a hard "US-only" transfer clause; instead, propose US-first + transfers only on instruction or with documented safeguards.

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear redlines — appreciate the detail. We reviewed with our legal and security leads and can accept most of Acme's requests with the following agreed language and operational commitments:

1) Transfers: Redwood will store customer data in U.S. regions by default. Transfers outside the U.S. will occur only: (i) on your documented instruction, or (ii) where necessary for operational continuity (e.g., failover), in which case we will apply contractual safeguards and report the transfer within 5 business days.

2) Subprocessors: We agree to provide 30 days' prior notice before onboarding a new subprocessor. Emergency security/patching exceptions will be permitted where we provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable and no later than 5 business days. We will also provide a monthly consolidated subprocessor list and a portal view for current subprocessors.

3) Opt-out / regulated categories: We are willing to accept Acme's ability to object to specific subprocessors for narrowly defined regulated data categories (e.g., health or regulated financial records). For general-purpose infrastructure (CDN, telemetry, monitoring) we will not permit opt-outs.

4) Access/deletion SLA: Contractually we propose a 60-day maximum cure window; operationally we commit to target 45 days and to publish metrics in the Redwood Console.

5) Audit evidence: We will provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and our security questionnaire.

I've attached an updated addendum that reflects these points. If that aligns, please sign via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/transactions/abc123.
